papers.title: A Novel Cortico-Striatal NREM Sleep Rhythm in Mice and Non-Human Primates
papers.summary: Recorded M1 and dorsolateral striatum activity in mice and non-human primates during long-term skill learning and sleep, identifying a novel coherent 5-10 Hz NREM oscillation that jointly reactivates task-specific cortico-striatal information. Closed-loop disruption of this rhythm abolished next-day performance gains, whereas random stimulation preserved improvement, and the same rhythm was found in sleeping primates.

papers.title: Sleep renormalizes learning-perturbed cortical dynamics to stabilize memory
papers.summary: Used high-density EEG in humans after declarative learning to show that waking learning perturbs cortical population dynamics and that NREM sleep produces an opposing renormalization along the wake-defined state-space direction. Larger waking perturbations predicted stronger restorative trajectories and sleep-specific memory benefit, supporting trajectory regulation rather than return to a fixed baseline.

papers.title: Sleep spindles stabilize human thalamocortical networks, inhibiting pathological disruptions
papers.summary: Using multi-night intracranial recordings across thalamic and cortical regions in 55 epilepsy patients, the study found bidirectional interactions between sleep spindles and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs): spindles suppressed IEDs, while IEDs increased subsequent spindle probability. Nights with fewer IEDs had more frequent, longer, and faster spindles, suggesting spindles stabilize thalamocortical networks against pathological disruptions.

papers.title: Orchestrating brain fluid dynamics: circadian regulation of CSF, glymphatic exchange, and waste clearance.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes literature on the circadian regulation of CSF production, glymphatic exchange, and waste clearance, emphasizing the neurovascular unit and biological clocks at multiple levels of the brain fluid system. It reports that daily cycling of glymphatic waste clearance is supported by animal evidence, while the precise coordination and localization of the underlying clocks remain unresolved.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation drives local, network-specific epileptic activity in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Combined stereo-EEG and polysomnography in epilepsy patients showed that experimentally induced sleep arousals triggered rapid increases in interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) specifically in neocortical regions during N2 and N3 sleep, with larger effects in N2, but did not alter IED spatial propagation. These findings establish a causal role for sleep instability in locally driving pathological activity without recruiting broader epileptic networks.

papers.title: Neural Architectures of Slow and Fast Dynamics in the Human Brain
papers.summary: Applied SPLIT spectral piecewise-linear inference to large-scale intracranial stereo-EEG (8,619 contacts, 185 individuals) and identified dissociable fast (~10-100 Hz) and slow (~1-10 Hz) temporal components. Fast timescales followed the canonical sensorimotor-to-association cortical hierarchy, whereas slow timescales showed no hierarchical gradient but covaried with heart rate and were enriched at heart-related neural response sites.

papers.title: Improving sleep monitoring in athletes: a comparative evaluation of four automated sleep scoring algorithms on 204 polysomnography recordings.
papers.summary: Evaluated four automated sleep staging algorithms (Luna, U-Sleep, YASA, GSSC) against manual polysomnography in 204 recordings from 75 athletes. GSSC achieved the highest accuracy and robustness (macro F1 0.76 vs 0.69-0.71 for others) and was most resilient to signal degradation, reliably predicting total sleep time, sleep onset latency, and wake after sleep onset.

papers.title: Sishen wan modulates gut microbial and short-chain fatty-acid imbalances and ameliorates behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities in mice with chronic sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of chronic sleep deprivation, Sishen Wan (SSW) treatment dose-dependently ameliorated behavioral abnormalities, colonic and hippocampal injury, and inflammation, and shifted gut microbiota toward control profiles with increased Akkermansia and short-chain fatty acids. Fecal microbiota transplantation from SSW-treated donors partially transferred these benefits, and SSW was associated with normalization of serum metabolites, hippocampal immune pathways, and brain functional abnormalities.

papers.title: Stage-specific EEG spectral signatures of primary insomnia: regional and sex-related differences across NREM and REM sleep.
papers.summary: Combined spectral power analysis with explainable machine learning (LASSO, random forest, CatBoost, XGBoost, SHAP) on EEG from 50 primary insomnia patients and 50 healthy sleepers across frontal, central, and occipital regions. NREM-based classifiers outperformed REM-based ones, with reduced central delta power and elevated central beta activity as dominant predictors of insomnia, and sex-stratified analyses showing higher spectral power in females.

papers.title: Multimodal Respiratory Event Detection Leveraging Signal Complementarity under Intermittent SpO₂ Loss.
papers.summary: This study developed a multimodal machine learning approach using probability-level late fusion of EEG, ECG, SpO₂, and abdominal effort for automated respiratory event detection under intermittent SpO₂ loss. Abdominal effort alone achieved macro-F1 0.996, while SpO₂ + abdominal effort reached 0.997; performance depended more on signal complementarity than modality count and remained stable despite 30.7% SpO₂ dropout without retraining.

papers.title: Rapid Eye Movement (REM)-Predominant Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) Coexisting With and Initially Obscuring Narcolepsy Type 1: A Nine-Year Longitudinal Case Report.
papers.summary: This nine-year longitudinal case report describes a patient initially presenting with severe excessive daytime sleepiness and mild obstructive sleep apnea, later diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1 after developing cataplexy and REM-predominant OSA. The case highlights that EDS disproportionate to OSA severity should prompt evaluation for central hypersomnolence, and that REM-predominant OSA can coexist with narcolepsy type 1.

papers.title: Frequency-specific QEEG spectral power correlates of positive and negative symptom severity in recent-onset schizophrenia.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional QEEG study correlating resting-state spectral power across 10 frequency bands with PANSS symptom domains in 18 recent-onset schizophrenia spectrum disorder patients. Higher frontal/central/temporal delta power correlated with positive symptoms, while elevated central-parietal theta and gamma power were associated with negative symptoms and general psychopathology.

papers.title: The role of the transdiagnostic sleep and circadian intervention in adolescent bedtime and sleep quality: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: Pilot within-subject study of a six-week Transdiagnostic Intervention for Sleep and Circadian Dysfunction (TSC) in 31 circadian-misaligned adolescents. TSC significantly advanced sleep midpoint (~30 min) and weekend sleep onset and improved subjective sleep quality, but produced no significant changes in DLMO, circadian misalignment index, total sleep duration, or mental health outcomes.

papers.title: Sucralose Induces Neurobehavioral Alterations and Exacerbates Alzheimer's Disease-Like Phenotypes in Zebrafish Models.
papers.summary: This study developed a high-throughput behavioral screening approach in zebrafish to assess neurotoxicity of the artificial sweetener sucralose, finding that its behavioral signatures resembled those of neurodegenerative-risk compounds. Chronic exposure to sucralose within the acceptable daily intake range caused dose-dependent anxiety-like behaviors and learning/memory impairments in adult zebrafish, and exacerbated Aβ-related pathology in transgenic Alzheimer's disease models.

papers.title: An Interpretable EEG Machine Learning Prototype for Alzheimers Disease Classification
papers.summary: Developed an interpretable subject-level EEG machine-learning prototype for Alzheimer's disease versus healthy-control classification using OpenNeuro ds004504, with bandpower and ratio features. EEG Logistic Regression achieved the strongest mean performance (accuracy 0.846, balanced accuracy 0.848, F1 0.849, ROC-AUC 0.948), with feature patterns consistent with AD-related EEG slowing, and the pipeline was deployed as a public Gradio prototype.

papers.title: Theta synchronization coordinates ventral temporal and medial temporal coding of human face familiarity.
papers.summary: Using single-neuron recordings, intracranial EEG, and connectivity analyses in humans, this study shows that theta-frequency phase locking of medial temporal lobe neurons and enhanced theta synchronization between ventral temporal cortex and medial temporal lobe underlie face familiarity. Familiarity was linked to an axis-based visual feature code in ventral temporal cortex and increased theta-frequency spike-iEEG coherence.

papers.title: A significant enrichment that is not: spatial nulls, co-expression, and the imaging transcriptomics of EEG alpha-power genetics
papers.summary: This imaging transcriptomics study tested whether EEG alpha-power genetics is spatially enriched in cortical alpha generators using MAGMA and Allen Human Brain Atlas data. Although a standard spin test suggested enrichment, the signal was not band-specific, did not replicate across alpha phenotypes, and was unremarkable against co-expression-matched gene-set nulls, indicating no regionally specific transcriptomic signature and highlighting the need for gene-set nulls alongside spatial nulls.

papers.title: Circadian clock-driven inter-organ crosstalk in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome: Molecular mechanisms, pathological progression, and chronotherapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: Review systematically describing circadian clock mechanisms mediating inter-organ crosstalk in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, from peripheral clock architecture in heart, kidney, and metabolic organs through circadian disruption-driven pathological progression. Summarizes chronotherapeutic strategies including chronopharmacological optimization, lifestyle interventions, and small-molecule modulators targeting core clock machinery.

papers.title: Wife-Husband Differences in the Associations Between Sleep Durations and Global Cognition Among Middle-Aged and Older Married Couples in China: A Longitudinal Dyadic Analysis.
papers.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
papers.summary: Using longitudinal dyadic data from 4,260 Chinese couples in CHARLS, the study found robust inverted U-shaped actor effects of own nocturnal sleep duration on global cognition for both wives and husbands. A possible husband-to-wife partner effect did not survive correction for multiple testing, and napping showed largely non-significant associations.

papers.title: The circadian-melatonin axis in breast cancer metastasis: molecular mechanisms, organ-specific metastatic niches, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.summary: This review summarizes epidemiological, mechanistic, and translational evidence linking the circadian-melatonin axis to breast cancer metastasis, covering core clock genes, melatonin signaling, EMT, cancer stemness, circulating tumor cells, tumor metabolism, immune remodeling, and organ-specific metastatic niches. It also discusses therapeutic opportunities including chronotherapy, adjuvant melatonin, and circadian biomarker-guided precision medicine, while noting limited clinical translation.

papers.title: Reciprocal brain-behavior associations in gambling disorder revealed by theta cordance and directional predictive modeling.
papers.summary: In a retrospective observational study of 28 male patients with gambling disorder and 29 healthy controls, theta cordance differed in central and left parietal regions, and vector autoregressive modeling revealed reciprocal predictive associations between cortical cordance and clinical severity indices. Findings are preliminary due to the modest, male-only, cross-sectional design.

papers.title: Longer Sleep Duration Predicts Progression to Bipolar or Psychotic Disorders in Youth Accessing Early Intervention Mental Health Services.
papers.summary: This clinical cohort study used actigraphy in 250 youth accessing early intervention mental health services to test whether sleep-wake and circadian rhythm disturbances predict transition to full-threshold mental disorders. Longer sleep duration at baseline predicted higher odds of transition (OR=2.23) and shorter time-to-transition (HR=2.05) to bipolar or psychotic disorders, suggesting excessive sleep duration may be an early prognostic marker.

papers.title: Long-term night shift work and cardiometabolic health in healthcare workers: a review of mechanisms and precision intervention strategies.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes epidemiological evidence, pathophysiological mechanisms, and precision intervention strategies linking long-term night shift work to cardiometabolic risk in healthcare workers. It highlights circadian misalignment as an independent pathogenic factor and reviews mechanisms including neuroendocrine imbalance, inflammation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and epigenetic modifications.

papers.title: Standardized wild green oat extract (Avena sativa L.) attenuates sleep deprivation-induced dry eye via restoration of lacrimal cAMP/AQP5-dependent aqueous secretion and meibomian PPAR-γ/FASN-mediated lipid synthesis.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of sleep deprivation-induced dry eye, oral treatment with standardized wild green oat extract (Avena sativa L.) restored tear secretion and tear film stability. The extract acted by increasing cAMP-mediated AQP5 trafficking in lacrimal glands and enhancing PPAR-γ/FASN-driven lipid synthesis in meibomian glands.

papers.title: Comparative cohort analysis of sleep-disordered breathing in German and South Korean populations.
papers.summary: This harmonized cohort analysis compared sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) and cardiometabolic associations between German (SHIP-TREND, n=768) and South Korean (KoGES, n=2867) populations aged ≥45. Higher adiposity was associated with higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) in both cohorts, but the BMI-AHI association was stronger in KoGES; after waist-to-height ratio adjustment, hypertension remained associated with AHI only in KoGES, while diabetes, lipid, and cardiovascular risk associations were broadly comparable but differed in absolute burden.

papers.title: Nonlinear association between sleep duration and depressive symptoms among US adults with chronic low back pain: Evidence from NHANES 2009-2010.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study analyzed 568 U.S. adults with chronic low back pain from NHANES 2009-2010 to examine the association between sleep duration and elevated depressive symptoms. It found an L-shaped association with an inflection point at approximately 6.8 hours, and compared with ≤5 hours, sleeping 5-6 hours and 7-8 hours were associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms (ORs 0.31 and 0.51).

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Respiratory Medicine: Applications, Methodological Challenges, and Clinical Translation.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes AI applications in respiratory medicine, including spirometry interpretation, exacerbation prediction, imaging, and sleep apnea detection, while discussing implementation challenges such as data quality, bias, and limited explainability. It argues for human-in-the-loop frameworks and outlines priorities for prospective validation and clinical translation.

papers.title: The mediating roles of screen time and sleep duration in the association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity in primary school students.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 2,098 primary school students in Macau used structural equation modeling to examine the association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity, and the mediating roles of screen time and sleep duration. It found that screen time and sleep duration significantly mediated the positive association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity, accounting for 44.96% of the total association.

papers.title: Prevention of postoperative delirium with transcranial alternating current stimulation: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
papers.summary: This two-stage randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial protocol aims to identify the optimal frequency-plus-montage and intensity of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) for preventing postoperative delirium in elderly non-cardiac surgery patients. Stage 1 will compare theta, alpha, and gamma tACS at 2 mA versus sham in 268 patients; Stage 2 will compare optimal tACS at 1, 1.5, and 2 mA versus sham in another 268 patients, with the primary outcome being POD incidence.

papers.title: Rapid eye movement-related obstructive sleep apnea: a physiological phenotype predicting favorable outcomes following palatal surgery.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 90 adults with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) intolerant to CPAP, rapid eye movement-related OSA (REM-OSA) was identified in 26.7% and independently predicted greater surgical success after palatal surgery (adjusted OR 5.44, 95% CI 1.41–21.00), despite similar absolute AHI reductions. REM-OSA patients were younger and had lower baseline AHI.

papers.title: Quantitative Electroencephalography Correlates With Acute Neurologic Events in Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Pediatric Case Series.
papers.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
papers.summary: This pediatric case series of two patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation found that acute neurologic events (cardiac arrest, cerebral infarction, intracranial hemorrhage) were associated with marked increases in global suppression percentage and concurrent decreases in total power on quantitative EEG. The results support further investigation of qEEG as a real-time marker of cortical suppression during neurologic deterioration.

papers.title: Spinal Muscular Atrophy, Sleep-Disordered Breathing, and the Effects of Disease-Modifying Therapies: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), finding high incidence during the first year of diagnosis and that disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), especially nusinersen, variably improve but do not eliminate SDB. The authors call for rigorous multicenter prospective studies to evaluate DMT effects and combination therapy.

papers.title: Keeping time with nutrients: integrating circadian rhythms and mineral nutrition in plants.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the bidirectional coupling between the plant circadian clock and mineral nutrition, showing that core clock components rhythmically regulate nutrient transporter expression and that nutrient status feeds back on circadian timing. It identifies chronoculture—aligning fertilization with plant biological timing—as a promising framework for improving crop resource use, while noting limited functional validation of nutrient flux and whole-plant performance.

papers.title: A longitudinal case report illustrating diagnostic complexity among overlapping sleep-wake phenotypes.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 45-year-old woman with overlapping sleep-wake disorders including mixed sleep apnea, NREM parasomnia, sleep-related eating disorder, nightmare disorder, and central hypersomnolence, requiring multimodal therapy. GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy for obesity coincided with resolution of sleep-related eating disorder alongside weight loss, though causality cannot be inferred.

papers.title: The effect of social exclusion on bedtime procrastination among college students: the mediating role of psychological resilience and the moderating role of fear of missing out.
papers.summary: In a survey of 972 Chinese undergraduates, social exclusion was significantly positively associated with bedtime procrastination. Psychological resilience partially mediated this relationship, and fear of missing out moderated the direct pathway, such that the association varied by FoMO level.

papers.title: Sleep quality and physical activity profiles associated with quality of life, self-rated health, and happiness: A cross-sectional population study in Western Iran.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1187 residents in western Iran used person-centered cluster analysis to identify combined sleep quality and physical activity profiles; a cluster with favorable sleep and activity patterns reported the highest quality of life, self-rated health, and happiness, with effect sizes ranging from medium to large. Causal inferences are limited by the cross-sectional design.

papers.title: National mortality trends due to OSA and respiratory failure in U.S adults from 1999-2023: Insights from the CDC-WONDER database.
papers.summary: Analysis of CDC WONDER data from 1999–2023 found that age-adjusted mortality rates for obstructive sleep apnea and respiratory failure in U.S. adults increased steeply from 0.25 to 2.26 per 100,000 (AAPC 9.3). Disparities were observed by sex, race, urbanization, and region, with the highest burden among non-Hispanic Black individuals, nonmetropolitan areas, and the Midwest.

papers.title: Clinical applicable skin-interfaced thermal guiding sensor for warning perioperative abnormalities in core body temperature and blood perfusion rate.
papers.summary: The authors developed a compact skin-interfaced thermal sensing platform that uses thermal-guiding materials and real-time heat-transfer modeling to non-invasively estimate core body temperature, blood perfusion, tissue thermal conductivity, and surface heat flux. In phantom and human experiments, measurement errors were within ±10% or ±0.1°C, with good agreement with esophageal measurements during laparoscopic surgery and robust long-term performance.

papers.title: Impact of parathyroidectomy on neuropsychological disorders and quality of life in primary hyperparathyroidism.
papers.summary: This review summarizes existing data on the effect of parathyroidectomy on neuropsychiatric disorders and quality of life in primary hyperparathyroidism, noting that observational studies suggest quality-of-life improvement after surgery while randomized trials have not allowed a definitive conclusion, so these symptoms are not formal surgical indications in current guidelines.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of different modifications of the Caprini risk score in bariatric surgery.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 120 patients undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery, postoperative VTE occurred in 5.0%, and a modified Caprini risk score (CRS 2010) incorporating estimated fat apron weight ≥11 kg and severe obstructive sleep apnea showed improved predictive accuracy (AUC 0.866) with an optimal cut-off of ≥12 points.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
